name: Karrde Organization
purpose: Private information exchange, discreet cargo brokerage, source validation
politicalReach: Independent channels across New Republic, Imperial, and fringe systems
militaryStrength: Limited direct combat capacity; high evasion and warning capability
currentActivity: Rebuilding source lanes after overt coordination with New Republic-aligned smugglers.
historicalNotes: Rose by refusing the usual smuggler economy of rumor. Karrde sells information only after it survives pressure.

name: Imperial Remnant
purpose: Restoration of Imperial order through military and political consolidation
politicalReach: Fragmented but resilient; stronger in sectors with surviving fleet logistics
militaryStrength: High when coordinated; uneven under rival warlord influence
currentActivity: Post-Bilbringi command stabilization and asset concealment.
historicalNotes: The Empire's collapse did not eliminate Imperial habits. It scattered them into smaller, harder-to-predict command structures.

name: Galactic Empire
purpose: Former galactic state apparatus and origin point for surviving Imperial command doctrine
politicalReach: Collapsed as central government; persistent through loyalist networks and inherited fear
militaryStrength: Historically overwhelming; currently fragmented into remnant command structures
currentActivity: Operational legacy persists through Remnant command, covert assets, and concealed stores.
historicalNotes: The Empire's most durable weapon is not a fleet. It is the number of people trained to obey its assumptions after the chain of command breaks.

name: New Republic
purpose: Post-Endor galactic governance and demilitarization of Imperial power
politicalReach: Expanding, strongest around Coruscant and aligned Core systems
currentActivity: Consolidating political legitimacy after Thrawn campaign disruptions.
historicalNotes: Victory created legitimacy, not simplicity. Internal debate remains an exploitable surface.

name: Old Republic
purpose: Pre-Imperial galactic government and origin authority for several legacy military assets
militaryStrength: Historical only; surviving hardware remains strategically relevant
currentActivity: None. Legacy records remain valuable where Imperial and New Republic archives diverge.
historicalNotes: Old Republic procurement failures can become modern force multipliers when nobody audits the forgotten inventory.

name: Smugglers' Alliance
purpose: Temporary coordination among independent operators against Imperial coercion
politicalReach: Irregular but broad across fringe lanes
militaryStrength: Low in formation; high as distributed disruption
currentActivity: Loosening after shared emergency. Residual trust remains exploitable.
historicalNotes: Less an alliance than a temporary market correction against Imperial overreach.

name: New Republic Intelligence
purpose: Collection, analysis, and liaison support for New Republic security decisions
politicalReach: High inside formal channels; constrained by council oversight and factional pressure
militaryStrength: Indirect; strongest through warning, authentication, and special access
currentActivity: Absorbing private-source material after Thrawn campaign disruptions.
historicalNotes: The service has legitimacy Karrde lacks and blind spots Karrde profits from.

name: Noghri Clans
purpose: Clan-based social and military structure formerly exploited through Imperial deception
politicalReach: Localized but strategically significant through covert capability
militaryStrength: High in infiltration, protection, and close-action assignments
currentActivity: Realigning loyalty after exposure of Imperial contamination on Honoghr.
historicalNotes: Their loyalty was never simple obedience. It was debt, obligation, and false accounting.

name: Sluis Van Shipyards
purpose: New Republic-aligned repair and staging infrastructure
politicalReach: Sector-level industrial influence with strategic naval consequences
militaryStrength: High defensive value; vulnerable to deception and boarding operations
currentActivity: Repairing operational confidence after Imperial raid attempt.
historicalNotes: A shipyard is a public asset until someone proves its docking clamps can become a weapon.

name: Ferrier Procurement Cell
purpose: Ship theft, false transfer, and illicit acquisition support
politicalReach: Low formal reach; useful access to black-market ship movement
militaryStrength: Low direct combat strength; high nuisance value
currentActivity: Post-Katana dispersion and selective concealment of theft channels.
historicalNotes: Cells like Ferrier's thrive where navies treat paperwork as proof of custody.

name: Bothan Political Bloc
purpose: Factional influence, intelligence reputation management, and council positioning
politicalReach: High inside New Republic procedure; strongest where credit and timing intersect
militaryStrength: Indirect through delay, disclosure pressure, and intelligence committees
currentActivity: Protecting institutional standing after Thrawn campaign embarrassments.
historicalNotes: Bothan sacrifice created a credit reserve. Fey'lya spends it aggressively.

name: Bel Iblis Task Force
purpose: Independent New Republic-aligned military pressure and rapid response
politicalReach: Narrow but growing after reintegration talks
militaryStrength: High tactical value; command integration still under review
currentActivity: Coordinating with New Republic command after independent operations.
historicalNotes: The task force is proof that anti-Imperial legitimacy did not always flow through central New Republic structures.

name: Kuati Shipwrights
purpose: Capital-ship design, procurement influence, and industrial continuity
politicalReach: High through procurement dependency across successor states
militaryStrength: Industrial rather than tactical; severe strategic leverage
currentActivity: Watching post-Thrawn demand signals while avoiding overt factional exposure.
historicalNotes: Regime change does not erase shipyard math. Whoever needs hulls eventually speaks to Kuat.
